speaker: Teacher (āgama-prāmāṇya)
question: What has just been concluded?
premises: Thus the whole, permanent, occasion-bound rite is established.
inference: The nitya-naimittika-karma exposition closes: the whole rite-class is nirūpita.

speaker: Teacher (āgama-prāmāṇya)
question: What is announced now?
premises: Now the authority of this very tradition is stated.
inference: The discourse turns from rite to prāmāṇya: āgama's authority takes the floor.

speaker: Teacher (āgama-prāmāṇya)
question: What makes something scripture?
premises: In the consciousness-made universe, vimarśa's sound-nature established, whatever contemplation of the world-thing and its act-fruit manifoldness that is — that is scripture.
Whole scripture is one-fruit-attaining by one-duty-declaration; yet people's rūḍhi stands part-by-part by the Lord's niyati-śakti.
inference: Śāstra is defined as vimarśana of the established world: structurally one-fruit, pedagogically part-graded by the Lord's necessity-power.

speaker: Teacher (āgama-prāmāṇya)
question: Where are the one-fruit attainments seated?
premises: Some in Veda-āgama scripture (Māyā-difference self), others Sāṃkhya-Vaiṣṇava, others Śaiva-Siddhānta, others Maṅgala-āgama, some rare in Trika's reflected Lord-nature, some by earlier-abandonment or transcendence.
All from one āgama alone: ekaphalasiddhi.
inference: Each school's rūḍhi sits in its own scripture, yet the single fruit issues from one āgama — school plurality does not multiply the fruit.

speaker: Teacher (āgama-prāmāṇya)
question: Does difference-doctrine cancel scripture's authority?
premises: In bheda-vāda too — all scriptures being one Lord's work — authority stands.
Partial agreement undenied, operation unstopped: mutual bādha from viśaya-bheda is akiṃcitkara.
inference: Even rival doctrines leave āgama's authority standing: contradiction by subject-difference alone is powerless.

speaker: Teacher (āgama-prāmāṇya)
question: How is āgama's prasiddhi rooted?
premises: Like brahma-killing-prohibition and ashrama-distinction: excellence follows fruit; in Upaniṣad-Bhāgavata distinct-authorship still conceivable, from meaning in what is said and beyond.
'I see gold, silver' — recognition through goldsmiths IS the āgama; child's engagement by recognition alone, inference-elimination absent in youth.
Rooted in recognition, some give impotence-dissolution-solitude fruits, some Siva-equality, some oneness-ending: whoever comes, force-of-heart recognition assumes it.
inference: Āgama's authority is prasiddhi-based (gold-silver by goldsmiths, child by seeing): recognition, not inference, roots it; and its fruits range severally to the heart's close.

speaker: Teacher (āgama-prāmāṇya)
question: What licenses the surplus verbal-connections?
premises: For the empty being's surplus vāc-yukti, any recognition taken as proof grants āgama-prāmāṇya; that āgama is relied on where utkṛṣṭa-phala is: enough by another.
inference: Surplus speech is licensed by any taken-as-proof recognition; the āgama is adopted where the excellent fruit stands — alam anyena.

speaker: Teacher (āgama-prāmāṇya)
question: How does the light behave?
premises: By consciousness-light-supreme-truth-nature, as it shines it touches also, so — discriminating.
inference: The paramārtha-light both manifests and contacts: the vivecana follows the double move.

speaker: Teacher (āgama-prāmāṇya)
question: Whose refuge is the scripture?
premises: Being, take refuge in the scripture — essence of all-made-consciousness-reflection-vimarśa, O Unsurpassable-self.
inference: The being is bidden to āśraya the śāstra whose sāra is the all-made vimarśa-nature — addressed to the anuttarātman.

speaker: Teacher (āgama-prāmāṇya)
question: What does the Prakrit verse declare?
premises: In the firm-establishment-made transaction, that very I am fearless.
inference: The Prakrit seal: in the vyavahāra of made-firm prasiddhi, the speaker is niṣaṅka.

speaker: Teacher (āgama-prāmāṇya)
question: What follows in the second Prakrit verse?
premises: Then you will be, according-as establishment-attained, Parama-Siva.
inference: Prasiddhi-attainment issues in Paramaśiva-tva: the verse promises the state conditionally.

speaker: Teacher (āgama-prāmāṇya)
question: What is asserted of the world?
premises: In own-firm-establishment-made transaction, the world is without doubt.
inference: The world's transaction, rooted in nija-ḍṛḍha-prasiddhi, stands niḥśaṅka — doubtless.

speaker: Teacher (āgama-prāmāṇya)
question: What does the āhnika close with?
inference: Closing seal: paramaśivatva achieved once the recognitions are crossed — the prasiddhi-series ends in the Lord.
